description: Input cases for tools/generate_onnx_golden_vectors.py. Each becomes one record in tests/data/onnx_golden_vectors.json. Most texts are taken from tools/golden_corpus.json by id, so the two golden files exercise the same lines; the rest are here because only a BERT-style tokenizer with role tokens makes them interesting. Plain data: add a case without touching code, then regenerate.

field_docs.name: Stable, unique, ASCII identifier. Never rename an existing name -- a Rust test may name it.
field_docs.role: 'passage', 'query' or 'raw'. The model input is '[PASSAGE] ' + text, '[QUERY] ' + text, or the text alone -- exactly what embedding text version 2 hands the backend for a stored passage and for a query, and a raw control with no role token at all.
field_docs.corpus_id: Take the text from tools/golden_corpus.json, by id, verbatim. Exactly one of 'corpus_id' or 'text' is required.
field_docs.text: The text itself, verbatim, without the role prefix. Invisible or ambiguous characters are written as \uXXXX escapes so a diff can show them.
field_docs.prefix_chars: Optional, with corpus_id: only the first N characters (code points) of the corpus text. How the token-boundary cases are cut from one long line.
field_docs.expect_total_tokens: Optional: the number of ids the golden must hold, after truncation. Pins a boundary; if a regeneration fails here, the tokenizer or the text changed. Recalibrate deliberately (--boundary-prefix), never relax.
field_docs.expect_untruncated_tokens: Optional: the number of ids the input tokenizes to with truncation off -- what proves a truncation case is truncated, and by how much.
field_docs.notes: What the case is for. Copied into the golden record.

cases.name: passage_heb_prose_mishneh_torah
cases.notes: Ordinary unpointed halachic prose: the common case, as a stored passage.

cases.name: passage_heb_prose_aggada
cases.notes: Ordinary unpointed aggadic prose.

cases.name: passage_aramaic_talmud_sugya
cases.notes: Talmudic Aramaic: a different language in the same script.

cases.name: passage_otzaria_line_with_reference
cases.notes: Title, reference and line, as an Otzaria line reads with its location written out.

cases.name: passage_punct_hebrew_abbrev
cases.notes: Geresh, gershayim, maqaf and sof pasuq in abbreviations.

cases.name: passage_punct_rashi_abbrev_dense
cases.notes: Commentary apparatus that is almost entirely abbreviations: the worst case for subword segmentation.

cases.name: passage_mixed_hebrew_english
cases.notes: Hebrew and Latin script in one line, with digits and '='. This normalizer does not lowercase -- 'Qwen3' reaches the model as written -- and it turns the em dash into '-'.

cases.name: passage_digits_and_gematria
cases.notes: Hebrew alphabetic numerals beside Western digits, joined by a maqaf.

cases.name: passage_final_letters
cases.notes: Final letter forms, which a normalizer must not fold into their medial forms.

cases.name: passage_invisible_bidi_marks
cases.notes: RLM, LRM, NBSP, ZWNJ, ZWJ and a soft hyphen. The normalizer removes the bidi and joiner marks, NFKC turns the NBSP into a space, and the soft hyphen survives: all invisible, so only the ids can show that the backend did the same.

cases.name: passage_whitespace_shapes
cases.notes: Tabs, newlines and runs of spaces inside the text.

cases.name: passage_near_identical_a
cases.notes: With passage_near_identical_b: two lines that differ by one word.

cases.name: passage_near_identical_b
cases.notes: With passage_near_identical_a.

cases.name: passage_unrelated_a
cases.notes: With passage_unrelated_b: same language, different domains.

cases.name: passage_unrelated_b
cases.notes: With passage_unrelated_a.

cases.name: passage_medium_paragraph
cases.notes: A responsa-length paragraph, inside the cap.

cases.name: passage_foreign_special_markup
cases.notes: Another model family's special-token markup (<|endoftext|>) in a paragraph. This tokenizer has no such token, so it is ordinary text here; the ids show it is not mistaken for one.

cases.name: passage_editorial_brackets
cases.text: אמר רבי יוחנן [משום רבי שמעון בן יוחאי] (ברכות ז, ב): גדולה שמושה של תורה יותר מלמודה, שנאמר (מלכים ב ג, יא) פה אלישע בן שפט [אשר יצק מים על ידי אליהו].
cases.notes: Otzaria-style editorial apparatus: a bracketed insertion and parenthesised source references inside a quotation.

cases.name: passage_editorial_gloss_nested
cases.text: ומברך על נטילת ידים (הגה: ויש אומרים שאין לברך עד שינגב [ועיין לעיל סימן ד, סעיף א], וכן נוהגין) (ב"י בשם הרא"ש).
cases.notes: A parenthesised gloss holding a bracketed cross-reference, then a parenthesised source abbreviation: nested apparatus, as commentaries print it.

cases.name: passage_literal_passage_marker
cases.text: בכתב היד נמצא הסימן [PASSAGE] באמצע השורה, ואחריו המשך הדברים.
cases.notes: The role marker itself inside the content. The tokenizer matches added special tokens anywhere in its input (encode_special_tokens is off), so the literal becomes the [PASSAGE] token a second time -- the reference does not escape or strip it, and the backend must not either: the ids pin that both sides treat it identically.

cases.name: passage_literal_bert_specials
cases.text: טבלה: [CLS] עמודה ראשונה [SEP] עמודה שנייה [MASK] ובסוף [UNK]
cases.notes: BERT's own special-token spellings inside the content. Matched as the special tokens they spell, like the role marker; a text that contains them is embedded with them, as the reference does.

cases.name: passage_literal_hebrew_markers
cases.text: הערת המהדיר [קטע] בתוך השורה, ואחריה [שאילתה] נוספת.
cases.notes: tokenizer.json also declares [שאילתה] and [קטע] as special tokens (ids 7 and 8), Hebrew spellings of the two roles; the recipe never produces them, but a line that contains them is matched to them, like [PASSAGE].

cases.name: passage_normalizer_classes
cases.text: אמר לו ‘כך מקובלני’ והשיב “ואני כך” – בסימן ３−１, כנזכר ב`ספר` ‫לעיל‬ ו⁦להלן⁩ מילה⁠בתוך﻿מילה​אחת, שׁבת וﭏהים ﬠל הכל ׆ נון הפוכה.
cases.notes: One character from each class the normalizer rewrites that the corpus lines do not already hold: curly single and double quotes and a backtick (to ' and "), an en dash and a minus sign (to -), bidi embedding and isolate controls, a word joiner, a zero-width space and a BOM (removed), a nun hafukha (U+05C6, removed with the pointing), fullwidth digits and Hebrew presentation forms (NFKC: the precomposed shin with its dot, whose dot the pointing rule then removes, the alef-lamed ligature, the alternative ayin). The rewrites are regular expressions, and the backend's tokenizer is built with a different regex engine (fancy-regex) from the Python reference's (onig): these ids are where the two would part.

cases.name: passage_over_256_truncated
cases.notes: A line far longer than the cap: truncated on the right to 256 ids in total, content first, so [CLS], the role token and the final [SEP] all survive.

cases.name: passage_boundary_exactly_256
cases.notes: Exactly 256 ids with nothing cut: the first 985 characters of over_512_full end on a whole word. An implementation that reserves one id too many, or counts the cap as content only, truncates this and changes its ids.

cases.name: passage_boundary_257_truncated_by_one
cases.notes: One character more -- the comma after that word -- is 257 ids, so exactly one content id is cut: the comma goes, and [SEP] stays last.

cases.name: raw_nikud_bereshit
cases.notes: Nikud as combining marks, with no role token. The normalizer removes the pointing, so the ids are those of the unpointed text.

cases.name: raw_teamim_shema
cases.notes: Cantillation marks, paseq and sof pasuq, with no role token. All are removed -- the paseq leaves two spaces behind, hence a lone '▁' id -- and sof pasuq goes with the pointing, before the rule that would have turned it into ':' sees it.

cases.name: raw_nikud_qamats_qatan
cases.notes: Rare pointing code points, qamats qatan (U+05C7, the end of the removed range) among them, with no role token.

cases.name: raw_heb_prose_mishneh_torah
cases.notes: The same text as passage_heb_prose_mishneh_torah and query_heb_prose_mishneh_torah, with no role token: the three differ only in the role.

cases.name: query_heb_prose_mishneh_torah
cases.notes: A stored line's text asked as a query: its ids differ from the passage's in the role token alone.

cases.name: query_two_words
cases.notes: A typical short search: two words.

cases.name: query_leading_whitespace
cases.notes: A query whose text begins with a space. The recipe prefixes '[QUERY] ' without trimming the query, so the model sees two spaces, and the Metaspace pre-tokenizer turns the extra one into a lone '▁' id after [QUERY] -- which '[QUERY]' + text, or a trimmed query, would not have. Passages cannot show this: the chunker trims them.

cases.name: query_single_word
cases.notes: One word.

cases.name: query_question
cases.text: מה הדין אם שכח לומר יעלה ויבוא בברכת המזון?
cases.notes: A whole question, as people type one.

cases.name: query_aramaic
cases.notes: An Aramaic query.

cases.name: query_mixed_script_digits
cases.notes: Latin, Hebrew and a digit in one query, beginning with a Latin letter; the same ids with or without the space after '[QUERY]'.

cases.name: query_starts_with_digit
cases.notes: Begins with a digit. Like every text that begins with something visible, it tokenizes to the same ids with or without the space after '[QUERY]'.

cases.name: query_starts_with_quote
cases.notes: Begins with a quotation mark; the same ids with or without the space after '[QUERY]'.

cases.name: query_starts_with_punctuation
cases.text: (ברכות ז, ב) גדולה שמושה של תורה
cases.notes: Begins with a parenthesis, as a pasted reference does; the same ids with or without the space after '[QUERY]'.

cases.name: query_lowercase_marker
cases.notes: The role marker in lower case inside the content. [QUERY] is declared with normalized: false, so only its exact spelling matches: '[query]' is tokenized as text.
